feedback.problem:
Find the solution of the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}12.8a+6.4=-6.4b \\ 2a+1=b\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}12.8a+6.4=-6.4b & |\,\times 10 \\ 2a+1=b & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}128a+64=-64b \\ 2a+1=b\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is already solved for $b:$

$$
b=2a+1
$$

Now, to find the value of $a,$ we can substitute $b=2a+1$ into the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}128a+64 & =-64b \\ 128a+64 & =-64(2a+1) \\ 128a+64 & =-128a-64 \\ 256a & =-128 \\ a & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ a & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $a=-0.5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+1 & =b \\ 2(-0.5)+1 & =b \\ -1+1 & =b \\ b & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-0.5$ and $b=0.$
